(i) the 13C spin state can be selected by the combination of Hadamard encoding of the multiple proton frequency and the use of pulsed‐field‐gradient echo; (ii) this method can be used for the selective excitation of 13C satellites in crowded 1H spectra; (iii) this method can also be applied to the measurement of small long‐range coupling constants.

we have developed new, improved NMR methods for selective excitation of 13C satellite lines, and demonstrated the utility of these methods in measuring long‐range proton‐carbon couplings in overcrowded 13C‐detected 1H N‐MR spectra.

we have demonstrated that the direct 13 C satellite‐selective excitations are possible and can be performed on a routine basis.

the 13C satellite lines can be directly and efficiently excited in crowded 1H NAR spectra by applying a combination of Hadamard‐phase encoded multiple‐proton excitation and pulsed field gradient‐echo techniques.
